Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme (since 2003, MoPNG): Roadmap 2020–25 moved E20 from 2030 → 2025 (achieved); E20 petrol mandatory nationwide from 1 April 2026 (RON 95); E20 = 20% ethanol (E100 = pure ethanol); no proposal at present to go beyond E20.
Current storage: 0.27 GW BESS, 7.2 GW pumped hydro.
Repo rate held at 5.25% in April 2026 – pause after ~125 bps cuts from early 2025; FY 2026–27 inflation estimate 4.6%. Governor Sanjay Malhotra.
Eurozone = 21 members – latest Bulgaria (2026); Croatia (2023).
Weak nominal GDP growth: ~8% (lowest in years) vs 10.1% assumed in the February 2025 Budget.
Bank infra bonds: RBI minimum maturity 7 years (typical 10–15); CRR and SLR exemptions; reduce asset–liability mismatch.
Rupee: full current account convertibility; capital account only partial.

Fishing grounds: The richest fishing grounds are where warm and cold ocean currents meet (e.g. Grand Banks off Newfoundland, the Kuroshio–Oyashio meeting area off Japan); the mixing brings up nutrients and plankton.
Projections: GDP current year 7.3% → 7.4%; next year 6.9–7%; inflation 2.1% → ~3.2%; next year 4–4.2%.

Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (MoSJE – Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar; 15 August 2020 in 272 districts, nationwide 2023; flagship of NAPDDR, run through NISD): reached 35.84 crore people (14.33 crore youth, 11.32 crore women) as on 10 Nov 2026 (29.32 crore in mid-2026).

MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes; launched 5 June 2023): extended to 2029 with ₹500 crore more (total ₹600 crore) (17 Jul 2026); AP ranked 2nd among States (30 Jul 2026).
Disbursed: 96 lakh loans worth ₹13,797 crore (30 July 2025); later 1.18 crore loans, ₹19,171 crore to 78.68 lakh vendors (PIB, as of 2026).

ODF Plus (as of 10 May 2023): 50% villages; large States – Telangana 100%, Karnataka 99.5%, Tamil Nadu 97.8%, UP 95.2%; small – Goa 95.3%, Sikkim 69.2%. Now: over 96% SBM villages ODF Plus (31 December 2025).
Justice Surya Kant: Chief Justice of India (August 2026 update).
[12 Aug 2026] CAG report tabled on drinking water, sanitation and passenger amenities at railway stations.
CAG: Article 148; appointed by the President; tenure 6 years or 65 years of age; Union audit reports go to the President, who lays them before Parliament.
SC reservation in legislatures: Arts 330, 332; periodically extended (latest up to 2030); no SC reservation in private-sector jobs.
PAC: 1-year term; examines CAG reports; chair usually from the Opposition.
24 February 2026, New Delhi – first in ~27 years (last 1999); CEC Gyanesh Kumar, ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
SC (2020): refused to transfer PM CARES money to NDRF; CAG audit applies to NDRF, not PM CARES.
Uptake: 31,555 employees as of 20 July 2025; last date to enrol 30 September 2025.
Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS): by the NSO, MoSPI; monthly and quarterly estimates since the January 2025 change in method (Current Weekly Status).

Expenditure Management Commission (Sept 2014): announced in the 2014-15 Budget, set up by Resolution; first Chairman (Cabinet rank) former RBI Governor Dr Bimal Jalan – not the BRICS NDB, whose first president was K.V. Kamath (source: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy 10th ed., part 06 p.30).

M. Narasimham Committees (banking reforms): Committee on the Financial System (1991) and Committee on Banking Sector Reforms (1998), both chaired by M. Narasimham; recommended lower SLR/CRR, entry of private banks and stronger capital adequacy norms.

23rd Law Commission: term 1 September 2024 – 31 August 2027; Chairperson Justice Dinesh Maheshwari (former SC judge), took charge 15 April 2025; full-time members Hitesh Jain and Prof. D.P. Verma; recommendations not binding; current mandate includes a Uniform Civil Code; no report released by November 2025.
22nd Law Commission (chair Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi, 2020–2024): the latest reports, numbered 278 to 289.
El Niño: warming of the central-eastern equatorial Pacific; Spanish for "Little Boy / Christ Child"; weakens trade winds, the Humboldt (Peruvian) Current and upwelling.
Drafts: first March 2014; six versions; the latest of those 31 Jul 2024 (valid till late July 2026).
The SC-appointed Central Empowered Committee (CEC) directed the AP government on illegal fish ponds in Kolleru WLS.
CEC assists the Supreme Court on forest and wildlife matters.

2025 athletics calendar (earliest to latest): 20th National Youth Athletics Championships, Patna (10–12 March) → 28th National Federation Senior Athletics Championships, Kochi (April) → Indian Grand Prix 2, Thiruvananthapuram (May) = order 2-3-1.
AP ranked 1st among Best Performing States for urban housing under PMAY-U 2.0 (2025–26); award on World Habitat Day, New Delhi.

Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) by IndiaTech.org with Consumer VOICE: AP ranked 1st for smooth used-vehicle ownership transfer, then Kerala, Tamil Nadu; Delhi 4th; Uttar Pradesh last; pre-owned vehicle market $36.4 bn (2024-25) → $73.5 bn (2030). *(news 10 Nov 2026)*
AP ranked 1st in utilisation of PM SHRI funds (reviewed by Nara Lokesh); PM SHRI = Prime Minister's Schools for Rising India – model government schools under NEP 2020 (not private).

CAG delegation (28 May 2025) at TUDA (Tirupati Urban Development Authority; statutory body under the AP Urban Development Authorities Act): recommended digitising financial and accounting systems; reviewed land acquisition, layouts, zoning, parks.

PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana – AP 4th in rooftop solar (after Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra): 7,39,260 households as of 15 Nov 2026, about 13% of 56.97 lakh nationally (Special CS Energy K. Vijayanand); Utility-Led Aggregation 68.9% (mainly SC/ST, DISCOM installs) vs CAPEX 31.1%; APSPDCL leads (2,00,196). Scheme: MNRE, Feb 2024, ₹75,021 crore, 1 crore households, up to 300 units free a month.

GSDP 2025-26 (advance estimates, current prices): ₹17.62 lakh crore (₹17,62,357 crore), up from ₹15.91 lakh crore = nominal growth 10.75% (above the national average; not 10.43%, which is the per capita income growth).
Q2 2025-26 growth: 11.28% vs all-India GDP 8.7% (current prices); The Hindu (Aug 2026) puts AP's growth over 2024-26 at 11.3% (Telangana 10.7%).
CAG: off-budget borrowings ₹1.28 lakh crore (March 2023, 9.7% of GSDP).
OTMPs handle nearly 50% of India's port cargo; AP ports = 16% of OTMP cargo; AP ranks 2nd after Gujarat (not first).
[26 Oct 2026] AP ranks 2nd in non-major port cargo traffic 2025-26 (DGCI&S); Gujarat 1st. AP ports handled about 210 MMT (about 12% growth).

8 Centre-funded projects, about ₹428 crore - heritage, beach, spiritual, Buddhist, river, eco-tourism. AP gave industrial status to tourism; new policy drew about ₹20,000 crore; AP's national tourism rank 16th → 13th.
LG AI Research: est. December 2020; HQ Seoul; research for 16 LG affiliates. EXAONE – LG's LLM series: EXAONE 1.0 first, EXAONE 4.0 latest.
new: LG AI Research: est. December 2020; HQ Seoul; research for 16 LG affiliates. EXAONE – LG's LLM series: EXAONE 1.0 first; **EXAONE 4.5 (Apr 2026, multimodal) latest** of the series; K-EXAONE (Jan 2026) = LG's sovereign-AI flagship.
why: EXAONE 4.5 (April 2026) and K-EXAONE (2026) have followed EXAONE 4.0.

text: AP international airports: three as of 2023 – Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati (APPSC 2023 question); Bhogapuram (Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport) opened Aug 2026. India: 16 international airports (as asked in a 2004 exam).
Exports over ₹150 crore in the current financial year – revival after Covid.
Exam angle: "who holds X as of <date>". Pawan Kalyan's portfolio has been asked before.
